correctness.rationale: For the quadratic FBE, direct substitution gives the feedback \(\ell_x(p)=a(1-s)(p^2-2p/s)/2\), hence the online update is the projected affine map \(p_{k+1}=\Pi_{[1,2/s-1]}(1/s+(1-\theta)(p_k-1/s))\). Every candidate in the interval contracts the primal step, so the null-step safeguard never fires. For \(0<\theta<2\), projection is inactive and the closed forms for \(p_k\) and \(x_k\) follow; \(\theta=1\) reaches the optimum on the second primal step. For \(\theta\ge2\), the projected map sends endpoints to opposite endpoints, producing the exact 2-cycle and linear absolute contraction. The repository exact-rational verifier checks representative regimes and the feedback identity; the symbolic projected-map analysis proves the complete range.
correctness.risk: The phase boundary depends on the specific candidate interval, initialization, scalar quadratic and constant online stepsize.

final_claim: For scalar OS-FBS on \(f(x)=a x^2/2\), \(g=0\), with \(s=\gamma a\in(0,1)\), candidate interval \([1,2/s-1]\), initial \(p_0=1\), zero regularization, and constant online stepsize, the dimensionless parameter \(\theta=\eta a(1-s)\) has a sharp transition at \(2\): for \(0<\theta<2\) the preconditioner converges geometrically to \(1/s\) and the primal iterates are Q-superlinear (with finite termination at \(\theta=1\)); for \(\theta\ge2\) the preconditioner alternates between the two interval endpoints and the primal iterates converge only linearly with factor \(1-s\).
limitations: The theorem does not extend the theta=2 threshold to multidimensional or nonquadratic problems.
